outcome: No new resolution of the problem has been found since 26 January 2024; the negative answer dates from January 2020 (MIP* = RE, arXiv:2001.04383), and the window holds a contested second route to a negative answer (Fang, Jiang, Wang and Wang, arXiv:2601.01733, January 2026, challenged by Pisier's February 2026 note), a second non-embeddable II1 factor (Manzoor, arXiv:2502.06697, February 2025), an AI-agent Lean formalisation of a core ingredient of the 2020 proof (FormalFlow, arXiv:2609.19814, September 2026), and AI-involved results on a different problem (Connes's rigidity conjecture, August 2026).
problem_asks: The bullet reads only 'Connes embedding problem in Von Neumann algebra theory', so the reading below is the standard one the name refers to (checked against the Wikipedia article, Goldbring's guided tour and Musat's overview). Part 1: does every II1 factor with separable predual embed (trace-preservingly) into the ultrapower R^omega of the hyperfinite II1 factor R? Part 2: the name also covers the wider form, whether every tracial von Neumann algebra with separable predual embeds into R^omega. Kirchberg's equivalence (every von Neumann algebra has the QWEP property) is a reformulation of Part 2, not a separate question. The bullet asks for a yes or no on existence of the embedding; it does not ask for an explicit embedding or an explicit counterexample.

events.what_happened: Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright and Yuen posted 'MIP*=RE' (arXiv:2001.04383). They prove that MIP* equals RE, and derive an efficient reduction from the halting problem to deciding whether a two-player nonlocal game has entangled value 1 or at most 1/2. Undecidability of the entangled value gives a negative answer to Tsirelson's problem. The abstract then says that, following Fritz (2012) and Junge et al. (2011), 'our results provide a refutation of Connes' embedding conjecture from the theory of von Neumann algebras'. The v1 argument used a two-prover low-degree test (Vidick 2016) that a later check found to be faulty; v2 (29 Sep 2020) replaced it with the quantum soundness of the classical low individual degree test (arXiv:2009.12982). The paper appeared in Communications of the ACM 64(11), November 2021 (DOI 10.1145/3485628, online 25 Oct 2021). The English Wikipedia article (opened) gives the same chronology: announced January 2020, error in an earlier cited result found September 2020, repaired preprint September 2020, CACM outline November 2021.
events.revisions: v1 13 Jan 2020 (two-prover low-degree test from Vidick 2016, later found faulty); v2 29 Sep 2020 (switches the argument to the low individual degree test, arXiv:2009.12982); v3 4 Nov 2022 (typos and presentation). Journal: Communications of the ACM 64(11), Nov 2021, pp. 131-138.
events.delivers: Negative answer to Part 1 (II1 factors with separable predual do not all embed in R^omega) and therefore to Part 2. The restriction is that the conclusion is by contradiction from undecidability: the chain is MIP*=RE, then undecidability of the entangled value, then failure of Tsirelson's problem (quantum tensor-product correlations not closed to quantum commuting ones), then failure of CEP via Fritz and Junge et al. The II1-factor form is stated explicitly by Goldbring and Hart (arXiv:2006.05629, event 2), not by this abstract.
events.remains: Nothing of Part 1 or Part 2 remains open as an existence question. Not settled by this event: an explicit non-embeddable algebra, which the bullet does not ask for.

checked_by.qualification: Model theorist working on operator algebras; not an author of MIP*=RE
checked_by.what_they_did: Wrote 'The Connes Embedding Problem: A guided tour' (arXiv:2109.12682), which introduces the background and outlines two proofs of the negative solution from MIP*=RE (one via Kirchberg's QWEP problem and Tsirelson's problem, one via logic). The notes present the derivation and do not claim a verification of the full 165-page argument.

events.doubts: (a) The v1 argument rested on a two-prover low-degree test from Vidick (2016) that a later check found to be wrong; the repair in v2 is a different test (arXiv:2009.12982). (b) The FormalFlow formalisation (event 16, Sep 2026) reports that it 'corrects side conditions and intermediate errors' in arXiv:2009.12982 while 'preserving the published final error bound under corrected assumptions'. This is a correction to stated hypotheses inside the repaired argument, not a withdrawal. (c) Zhao (event 15, Sep 2026) shows that a variant of the argument, replacing 'conditional linear functions' by 'coordinate deletion functions' and dropping the diagonal-lines subtest, is not sound; the abstract says the published argument is not thereby shown wrong. (d) Boaz Barak (Windows on Theory, 14 Jan 2020) says he is 'not an expert in this area' and that he still has to read the paper beyond its first few pages. No source read gives an expert verification of the full 2020 argument.
events.direction: Cuts against the conjecture: asserts that CEP fails, i.e. that not every II1 factor with separable predual embeds into R^omega.
events.object: No explicit object. The reduction takes a nonlocal game whose entangled value is undecidable (from the halting problem); the non-embeddable algebra is obtained by contradiction through the Tsirelson and Fritz/Junge chain. Non-constructive.

events.what_happened: Goldbring and Hart, 'The universal theory of the hyperfinite II1 factor is not computable' (arXiv:2006.05629). Using MIP*=RE and an earlier observation of the authors that CEP is equivalent to computability of the universal theory of II1 factors, they derive a negative solution to CEP that avoids the QWEP and Tsirelson equivalences. The introduction states: 'the main theorem here yields a proof that MIP*=RE implies that CEP has a negative solution'. Section 5 (Corollary 5.5, added in v3) gives infinitely many counterexamples. Listed as published in the Bulletin of Symbolic Logic (publication details not verified).
events.revisions: v1 10 Jun 2020; v2 15 Jun 2020; v3 21 Jun 2021 (adds the infinitely-many-counterexamples corollary, Section 5).
events.delivers: Negative answer to CEP stated for II1 factors (Part 1), with an argument that goes through the universal theory of R rather than the QWEP/Tsirelson route. Restricted to the MIP*=RE hypothesis, so it is not independent of event 1. Corollary 5.5 gives infinitely many non-embeddable II1 factors, per the paper's own description.
events.remains: Part 2 is covered by Part 1's failure. No existence question remains open. An explicit non-embeddable algebra is not supplied.
events.doubts: The argument depends on MIP*=RE and inherits the doubts recorded at event 1. No independent engagement with this paper was found beyond the authors' own expositions (events 3 and 7).
events.direction: Cuts against the conjecture: asserts CEP fails for II1 factors.
events.object: No explicit object. Non-computability of the universal theory of R gives, via the stated equivalence, a non-embeddable II1 factor by a non-constructive argument.

events.what_happened: Goldbring, 'The Connes Embedding Problem: A guided tour' (arXiv:2109.12682, 26 Sep 2021). Expository notes (comment: '74 pages. First draft.') that set out the background needed for the MIP*=RE route and outline two proofs of the negative solution: a 'traditional' route through Kirchberg's QWEP problem and Tsirelson's problem, and a second route using basic ideas from logic. The abstract states the CEP 'is a problem in the theory of tracial von Neumann algebras' and frames it for tracial algebras.
events.revisions: v1 only (26 Sep 2021). No later version found on the arXiv page.
events.delivers: No new result. Restates the negative solution from MIP*=RE, for the tracial von Neumann algebra form of CEP (Part 2), with a note that the II1-factor form is the usual formulation.
events.remains: No change to Parts 1 or 2 beyond event 1.
events.doubts: None specific to this exposition. It inherits the dependence on MIP*=RE.
events.direction: Cuts against the conjecture (restates the negative solution).

events.what_happened: Frei, 'Connes implies Tsirelson: a simple proof' (arXiv:2209.07940, 16 Sep 2022). Shows that the Connes embedding problem implies the synchronous Tsirelson conjecture, using standard trace descriptions of synchronous correlations and a lifting result of Kim, Paulsen and Schafhauser. It notes that the MIP*=RE refutation of the synchronous Tsirelson conjecture is by contradiction, so an explicit synchronous counterexample is open.
events.delivers: One direction of an equivalence: a positive answer to CEP implies a positive answer to the synchronous Tsirelson conjecture. It does not resolve CEP either way.
events.remains: Parts 1 and 2 untouched. The paper itself does not claim an explicit counterexample.
events.direction: Neutral to the status of the problem: an implication between two equivalent-in-the-literature questions, not a resolution.

The abstract page does not name CEP and does not claim a new negative answer.
events.delivers: No result on CEP that I could read from the abstract page; a survey whose bearing on CEP was not confirmed.
events.remains: All of Parts 1 and 2 (no existence result).
events.direction: Neutral: survey; no direction for the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Arulseelan, Goldbring and Hart, 'The undecidability of having the QWEP' (arXiv:2205.07102, first posted 14 May 2022, v2 27 Aug 2023). Shows that the class of C*-algebras with Kirchberg's QWEP property, and the class of W*-probability spaces with QWEP, are not effectively axiomatizable, and that the hyperfinite III1 factor and the Powers' factors have no computable universal theory. Listed as going to the Journal of Operator Theory.
events.revisions: v1 14 May 2022; v2 27 Aug 2023 (a minor mistake in Theorem 2.1 fixed, conclusion strengthened).
events.delivers: Not a result on the status of CEP. It concerns the logical complexity of the QWEP property, which Kirchberg's equivalence ties to Part 2, but the abstract does not state a consequence for CEP's truth value.
events.direction: Neutral to the conjecture: a result about QWEP classes, not about the embedding question.

events.what_happened: Bowen, Chapman, Lubotzky and Vidick, 'The Aldous-Lyons Conjecture I: Subgroup Tests' (arXiv:2408.00110, 31 Jul 2024). Refutes the Aldous-Lyons conjecture (every invariant random subgroup of a free group is co-sofic) by exhibiting a non co-sofic invariant random subgroup, using a tailored MIP*=RE reduction in a companion paper [BCV24] that I did not locate. The abstract does not mention Connes's embedding problem, hyperlinearity or II1 factors.
events.delivers: Negative answer to the Aldous-Lyons question about invariant random subgroups of free groups (co-sofic). Discounted for this bullet: it concerns invariant random subgroups and sofic approximation, not the embedding of II1 factors into R^omega.
events.remains: Parts 1 and 2 untouched by the abstract.
events.time_since_posted: 2 years 2 months (since 31 Jul 2024); uptake was not searched beyond the search results
events.doubts: The companion paper [BCV24] was not located, so the full chain was not checked.
events.direction: Neutral for this bullet: a negative answer on a neighbouring question (co-sofic invariant random subgroups).
events.object: A non co-sofic invariant random subgroup of a free group, obtained from a tailored non-local game. Non-constructive per the abstract's approach.

events.what_happened: Goldbring, 'Undecidability and incompleteness in quantum information theory and operator algebras' (arXiv:2409.08342, 12 Sep 2024). A survey of incompleteness results in operator algebras that follow from MIP*=RE, including what the author calls a 'Gödelian refutation of the Connes Embedding Problem' (Section 4.3, Theorem 4.9: 'Th-forall(R) is not computable, whence the CEP has a negative solution'). The paper says it surveys results, not that it proves new ones, and attributes the refutation to Goldbring and Hart's earlier work. It also discusses the Aldous-Lyons application.
events.delivers: No new result on CEP. Restates the negative solution via MIP*=RE and the Goldbring-Hart argument; the II1-factor form is the one used in its Section 4.3 statement.
events.direction: Cuts against the conjecture (restates the negative solution as established).

events.what_happened: Dogon and Vigdorovich, 'Hyperlinearity, stability and asymptotic spectral gap of higher rank lattices' (arXiv:2506.20843, v1 25 Jun 2025, v2 23 Jun 2026). Conditional result: if SL2(Z[1/p]) is flexibly Hilbert-Schmidt stable for some prime p, then it has a non-hyperlinear finite central extension. A positive answer to a question about representations of SL2(Z) agreeing on an Iwahori subgroup would give an explicit non-hyperlinear group. The question at issue is group-level hyperlinearity, not the embedding of II1 factors.
events.delivers: Conditional. Says nothing unconditional about CEP. For this bullet it concerns whether groups are hyperlinear, a different question from the embedding of II1 factors (Part 1), though the two are linked in the literature.
events.doubts: Conditional on an unproven stability statement; the abstract does not claim an unconditional non-hyperlinear group.
events.direction: Neutral for this bullet: conditional group-level result.

events.what_happened: Manzoor, 'There Is An Equivalence Relation Whose von Neumann Algebra Is Not Connes Embeddable' (arXiv:2502.06697, v1 10 Feb 2025; v2 4 Apr 2026, listed as 'to appear in Compositio Mathematica'). Theorem 1.1: there is a Property (T) ergodic countable probability measure preserving equivalence relation R such that the Property (T) II1 factor L(R) is not Connes embeddable. The construction uses a notion of hyperlinearity for invariant random subgroups of a free group and a simplified reduction to nonlocal games, which the paper says relies on the MIP*=RE machinery (via the tailored reduction of [BCV24]).
events.revisions: v1 10 Feb 2025; v2 4 Apr 2026 (listed as 'to appear in Compositio Mathematica').
events.delivers: A second counterexample to Part 1 in the II1-factor class: a Property (T) II1 factor arising as the von Neumann algebra of an equivalence relation. Restriction: it is a single algebra class, and it reaches non-embeddability through the MIP*=RE machinery, so it does not add a new route. It does not change the status of Parts 1 or 2, which are already negative.
events.remains: No part of Parts 1 or 2 is newly settled; they were already negative by event 1.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted for publication, per the arXiv comment 'to appear in Compositio Mathematica'. Referee reports are not public. The journal page was not opened.

events.doubts: Inherits the MIP*=RE dependency through the tailored reduction; the companion [BCV24] was not opened. The Acknowledgements thank Michael Brannan for proofreading only; that is not a verification. No specific error found.
events.direction: Cuts against the conjecture: a non-Connes-embeddable II1 factor (Part 1 fails).
events.object: L(R), the II1 factor of a Property (T) ergodic countable pmp equivalence relation R, built from a non-co-hyperlinear invariant random subgroup of a non-abelian free group. Existence argument; R is not written down explicitly.
people: Michael Brannan (thanked for proofreading, not a verifier)

events.what_happened: Fang, Jiang, Wang and Wang, 'Completely Bounded Representations Into Von Neumann Algebras And Connes Embedding Problem' (arXiv:2601.01733, first posted 5 Jan 2026; listed as v1 only when checked on 11 Oct 2026). Proves Theorem 1.4: if A is a unital separable C*-algebra, M a von Neumann algebra with QWEP, and phi a unital completely bounded representation, then some invertible S in M makes S phi(.) S^-1 a *-representation. Combined with Pisier's characterisation of nuclearity (their Theorem 1.3) and the assertion that the full C*-algebra of the free group on infinitely many generators is not nuclear (asserted, not proved in the introduction), they conclude that some von Neumann algebra is not QWEP, and by Kirchberg's equivalence that CEP has a negative answer. The abstract states: 'This provides a negative answer to the Connes Embedding Problem.' The argument relies on Pop (Integral Equations Operator Theory 89, 2017, 'Similarities of tensor products of type II1 factors') for Theorem 1.2.
events.revisions: v1 5 Jan 2026 only, as shown on the arXiv abstract page when checked on 11 Oct 2026.
events.delivers: Claims a negative answer to Part 2 via existence of a non-QWEP von Neumann algebra. Scope gap: the abstract does not say whether the non-QWEP algebra can be taken to be a II1 factor with separable predual, so Part 1 is not shown to fail by this route as stated. The claim depends on Pop's Theorem 1.2 as used, which event 13 says is faulty as used.
events.remains: Part 1 (II1 factors) is not addressed explicitly. Part 2 is claimed negative, subject to the Pop step and the asserted non-nuclearity of C*(F_infinity).
events.doubts: (a) Pisier's note (event 13, arXiv:2601.10654, v1 15 Jan 2026, v4 22 Feb 2026) says that a statement in Pop's reference [12] that is 'crucially used in [2]' is not valid, and that 'the application proposed in [2] to the Connes embedding problem' therefore fails. Pisier locates the error in an incorrect identification TBT^-1/J = S(B/J)S^-1, since (1-p)B need not equal J. (b) No reply, erratum or withdrawal found: the arXiv abstract page showed v1 only on 11 Oct 2026, and the searches for a response found none. (c) The introduction asserts that C*(F_infinity) is not nuclear and that Pisier's theorem yields non-QWEP algebras, without proof. (d) Single-version preprint, not peer reviewed. (e) The same negative answer was known from MIP*=RE in 2020, so the paper is an alternative route, not a new status change.
events.direction: Cuts against the conjecture (claims CEP fails, via a non-QWEP algebra).
events.object: No explicit algebra in the claimed deduction. The non-QWEP algebra is obtained non-constructively: if every von Neumann algebra were QWEP, Theorem 1.4 and Pisier's theorem would make every separable unital C*-algebra nuclear, contradicting non-nuclearity of C*(F_infinity).

events.what_happened: Pisier, 'A note on strong similarity and the Connes embedding problem' (arXiv:2601.10654). Constructs a unital completely bounded homomorphism u from C = C*(F_infinity) (which has the lifting property) into a QWEP von Neumann algebra N = B(H) tensored with M (M the vN algebra of the reduced group C*-algebra of F_infinity), such that u is not strongly similar to a *-homomorphism: the similarity cannot be chosen in N. Shows u has no completely bounded lift into a WEP C*-algebra of which N is a quotient. Proves a Haagerup/Paulsen-type formula for strong similarity. In the introduction and appendix it says that the statement from Pop [12] 'crucially used in [2]' (Fang et al.) is not valid, and that 'the error in [12] lies in an incorrect identification' (Appendix). Its own counterexample uses a QWEP target, so it does not settle CEP.
events.revisions: v1 15 Jan 2026; v2 22 Jan 2026; v3 12 Feb 2026; v4 22 Feb 2026 ('further expanded exposition, addition of a new proof of main point').
events.delivers: Not a CEP resolution. Establishes a counterexample to strong similarity in the QWEP setting and identifies a specific error in Pop's argument as used by Fang et al. Its bearing on the CEP status is only through the invalidation of the Fang et al. application.
events.remains: Parts 1 and 2 are not addressed as existence questions.

checked_by.qualification: Author of the similarity and nuclearity theory the Fang et al. argument invokes; a leading specialist in operator spaces and similarity problems
checked_by.what_they_did: Checked the Pop-based step used by Fang et al. and wrote that its identification is incorrect, so the claimed CEP application is not valid. The note itself makes no claim about CEP's truth value.

events.directly_checkable: The counterexample algebra and map: C*(F_infinity) to B(H) tensor M, a unital cb homomorphism not strongly similar to a *-homomorphism in N. Checkable from the stated construction in arXiv:2601.10654v4; the full argument was not re-verified here.
events.doubts: Explicitly unpublished, according to a search summary of the note that I did not verify on the abstract page. Versions differ (v4 adds a new proof of the main point), so the statement cited should be checked against the version used.
events.direction: Cuts against the Fang et al. route to a negative CEP answer (invalidates its application). Neutral on CEP itself.
events.object: A unital completely bounded homomorphism u: C*(F_infinity) -> N with N = B(H) tensor M QWEP, which is not strongly similar to a *-homomorphism inside N. Explicit algebras and map; non-similarity shown by argument.

events.what_happened: Zhao, 'The Low-Individual-Degree Test Without the Diagonal-Lines Test Is Not Quantum-Sound' (arXiv:2609.12346, 11 Sep 2026). Argues that the diagonal-lines subtest cannot simply be removed from the low individual degree test. Specifically, replacing 'conditional linear functions' by 'coordinate deletion functions' in the MIP*=RE proof does not by itself preserve soundness; the counterexample is for (m, d) = (2, 2) and any odd prime q. The abstract notes that JNVWY found an example that requires the diagonal-lines test.
events.delivers: Concerns a variant of the MIP*=RE argument, not the published argument. Per the abstract it does not say that arXiv:2009.12982 or MIP*=RE is wrong.
events.directly_checkable: The (m, d) = (2, 2) counterexample for the variant, for any odd prime q, as described in the abstract. The full construction was not read.
events.doubts: A critique of a variant. Whether the variant appears in any published proof is not established by the abstract. Full text not read.
events.direction: Neutral on the conjecture: a counterexample to a variant of a proof step.
events.object: A small counterexample showing the variant (with coordinate deletion functions and no diagonal-lines subtest) is not quantum-sound, for (m, d) = (2, 2) and any odd prime q.

events.what_happened: Lu, Deng, Zhu and Ji, 'Long-horizon autoformalization of a core theorem underlying MIP* = RE' (arXiv:2609.19814, v1 17 Sep 2026, v2 24 Sep 2026). Presents FormalFlow, 'a system that coordinates AI proving agents under human supervision', which produced a machine-checked Lean 4 proof of the quantum soundness of the classical low individual-degree test (the theorem of arXiv:2009.12982). The final library has 126,367 lines of Lean, 'all generated by agents', built in about 63 days. The abstract states that the formalisation 'corrects side conditions and intermediate errors while preserving the published final error bound under corrected assumptions'. A search summary of the paper (not verified on the abstract page) gives the specific change: the printed condition k >= md becomes k >= 400md, and the d = 0 case requires k > 0. The repository https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE follows the LDT paper and says it contains 'sorries' and 'axioms' badges whose values were not readable.
events.delivers: Claims a machine-checked Lean 4 proof of one core ingredient of MIP*=RE (the quantum soundness of the LID test) under corrected side conditions. It does not formalise MIP*=RE as a whole and does not formalise the CEP step.
events.remains: The rest of the MIP*=RE chain, including the reduction from RE and the Tsirelson / CEP step, is not formalised by this event. Whether the library is sorry-free is not stated in the abstract, and I did not establish it.
events.doubts: (a) Co-author Zhengfeng Ji is also a co-author of MIP*=RE and of the LID-test paper, so this is not independent. (b) The corrections change stated hypotheses of the LID-test theorem; the authors say the final bound is preserved under corrected assumptions, but the corrected statement's effect on the MIP*=RE chain was not checked here. (c) Sorry-free status not established. (d) Preprint, not peer reviewed.
events.direction: Supports the LDT ingredient under corrected hypotheses. Bears on the negative answer only through MIP*=RE.

The repository openai/ten-proofs links item 4 to ConnesRigidity.lean and describes it as 'a counterexample to the conjecture that certain groups are determined by their group von Neumann algebras'. This is Connes's rigidity (W*-superrigidity) question, not the embedding problem. Secondary coverage reports that the Lean certificates check formal correctness and that the paper is not yet peer reviewed.
events.revisions: None found for the announcement itself.
events.delivers: Not about CEP. Claims a counterexample to Connes's rigidity conjecture (groups determined by group von Neumann algebras). Discounted for this bullet: a different problem.

disputes.summary: Fang, Jiang, Wang and Wang (arXiv:2601.01733, 5 Jan 2026) claim a negative answer to CEP via a non-QWEP algebra, relying on Pop (IEOT 89, 2017). Pisier (arXiv:2601.10654, v1 15 Jan 2026, v4 22 Feb 2026) says a statement from Pop that Fang et al. 'crucially used' is not valid, and that the CEP application they proposed is therefore not valid. No reply, erratum or withdrawal was found by 11 Oct 2026, and the Fang et al. arXiv page showed v1 only.

Neighbouring problem, not CEP: OpenAI's Astra announcement (1 Aug 2026) and Zhou's arXiv:2608.02327 (3 Aug 2026) both claim counterexamples to Connes's rigidity conjecture using property (T) groups. A PhilArchive critique reported by ecosistemastartup.com (2 Aug 2026) says OpenAI's groups fail the ICC and property (T) hypotheses. The critique was not opened.

summary: The bullet asks whether every II1 factor with separable predual embeds in R^omega, and the name also covers the tracial form. The answer is negative, from Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright and Yuen's MIP*=RE (arXiv:2001.04383; v1 13 Jan 2020, v2 29 Sep 2020 repair, CACM Nov 2021). The English Wikipedia article (opened) gives the same chronology and has no 2024-2026 entries. Goldbring and Hart (arXiv:2006.05629, June 2020) give a second derivation that states the II1-factor form explicitly, and Goldbring's expositions (2021, 2024) present the negative solution as established; all of these trace back to the MIP*=RE chain. I found no new resolution since 26 January 2024. The in-window events are: (i) Manzoor (arXiv:2502.06697, Feb 2025; v2 Apr 2026, listed as to appear in Compositio Mathematica), a Property (T) II1 factor that is not Connes embeddable, which adds a counterexample but does not change the status; (ii) Fang, Jiang, Wang and Wang (arXiv:2601.01733, 5 Jan 2026), an operator-algebraic claim of a negative answer via Theorem 1.4, Pisier's nuclearity theorem and Pop's 2017 result. Pisier's note (arXiv:2601.10654, Jan-Feb 2026) identifies an incorrect identification in Pop's argument, as used by Fang et al., and says the CEP application is invalid; no reply appears on arXiv (v1 only as of 11 Oct 2026). The Fang et al. abstract does not say whether the non-QWEP algebra can be taken to be a II1 factor, so this route does not show Part 1 fails as stated. (iii) FormalFlow (arXiv:2609.19814, 17 Sep 2026), an AI-agent Lean formalisation of the quantum soundness of the low individual-degree test (arXiv:2009.12982), a core ingredient of MIP*=RE. It reports corrections to side conditions and intermediate errors while keeping the final error bound. Whether the library is sorry-free was not established. (iv) Zhao (arXiv:2609.12346, Sep 2026) shows that a variant of the LID-test argument (without the diagonal-lines subtest) is not sound; the abstract does not say the published argument is wrong. Other in-window items are group-level or neighbouring: Bowen-Chapman-Lubotzky-Vidick on Aldous-Lyons (2024), Dogon-Vigdorovich and Thom on hyperlinearity (conditional, 2025-2026), Musat and Goldbring's 2024 survey (expository), and the DeepMind formal-conjectures issue (2026, statement only). AI involvement: no AI system is named in any source read that bears on CEP's status (2020, 2022, 2024, 2025, Fang et al., Pisier), so none_found is true for those events. The AI involvement found is in FormalFlow (event 16, a close call: formalisation of a human proof, but with reported corrections of hypotheses) and in the neighbouring rigidity results (events 18-19), which are discounted for this bullet. OpenAI's own page returned 403, so the Astra authors' account is not recorded. Close calls: (a) whether FormalFlow's corrections make its AI work load-bearing; (b) whether Fang et al. establish the II1-factor form, which their abstract does not say; (c) whether the Pisier objection defeats Fang et al. entirely or only the step they cite. Several AI-specific searches on the CEP itself (including 'AlphaEvolve', 'GPT-5', 'Gemini', 'Claude', 'LLM', 'ChatGPT', 'Lean') found no AI result on it.
competing_reading: The window contains no change of status: the only resolution (MIP*=RE, 2020) predates it, and every in-window item either restates it, adds a counterexample in the same class, challenges a second route, or concerns a neighbouring problem. A reader who treats Fang et al. as an independent second resolution (it does not use MIP*=RE) would count one in-window resolution, although Pisier's note says its key step fails. A reader who treats FormalFlow as AI doing load-bearing mathematics (because it corrects hypotheses in a human proof) would count an AI contribution to the core of the 2020 chain; a stricter reader would count it as formalisation only.
what_would_settle_it: (1) A reply to Pisier's note, or a v2 of arXiv:2601.01733 that repairs or withdraws the Pop-based step, plus any erratum for Pop (IEOT 89, 2017). (2) The FormalFlow repository's sorry and axiom status, and whether the corrected side conditions (k >= 400md; k > 0 at d = 0) appear in the published version of arXiv:2009.12982, along with the corrected error bound. (3) Whether a non-QWEP algebra from Fang et al. can be taken to be a II1 factor with separable predual. (4) The Astra authors' own account of the rigidity result, and the PhilArchive critique. (5) Full texts of arXiv:2001.04383 and arXiv:2502.06697 for acknowledgements and AI statements, which I could not read through the fetch tool.

dead_ends: No AI system was found credited with work on the CEP itself. The AI hits were for other problems: Erdos unit-distance, Connes rigidity (Astra, Zhou), commutative algebra, convex optimisation.
No erratum or withdrawal found for MIP*=RE beyond the v1 to v2 replacement of the LDT ingredient.
No erratum found for Pop (IEOT 89, 2017) (three searches). No withdrawal or response found for arXiv:2601.01733.
No explicit counterexample to CEP or any 2026 construction of one found. Thom's and Pisier's notes are conditional or about strong similarity.
No Tao blog post or MathOverflow thread on this result found.
No complete Lean formalisation of MIP*=RE found. An EPFL student page lists it as a goal, and FormalFlow covers only the LID-test ingredient.

A ResearchGate listing claims a May 2026 preprint 'Model theory and Ultrapower Embedding Problems' (Kanovei, Katz, Kudryk, Kuhlemann) that it says gives strong evidence for a negative solution of the Kirchberg embedding problem. I could not find its arXiv record, so it is not recorded as an event.
mewayz.com blog posts on the CEP were read in search results and not used, as they are low-quality and loosely framed.

Pre-2024 reformulations seen only in search snippets (Fritz 2012; Junge et al. 2011; Ozawa 2013 on Tsirelson/QWEP; Harris 2017 on XOR games; Russell 2019 on synchronous correlations) are equivalences, not resolutions, and are not recorded as separate events.

judgement.why: MIP*=RE (Jan 2020) answers the yes/no question in the negative. I mark it digested: it went through a 2020 repair, appeared in CACM, and was worked through in Goldbring's exposition of the derivation. Goldbring–Hart is a second derivation from before the snapshot. Manzoor's non-embeddable Property (T) factor of an equivalence relation is a stronger counterexample to a conjecture already refuted (F4). It answers a strengthened question, not the open one, so I answer variant even though it was accepted by Compositio. Fang et al. claim the whole answer, but Pisier pins a specific, unanswered error on the Pop step they rely on, so it is knocked_down. FormalFlow formalises a human proof and does no new mathematics on CEP, so its AI role is none. Its corrections of side conditions apply to a proof ingredient, not to this problem. The rigidity results (Astra, Zhou) are a different problem: variant, with the AI role not carried over to CEP. Surveys, conditional group results, the issue and the critiques score none or variant.
judgement.doubts: Close call: should MIP*=RE count as digested? No source in the record says a named expert worked through all 165 pages, and the CACM version is a research-highlights outline. If it is unreviewed instead, the problem would fall to open rather than open_stale. Manzoor could also be read as a whole answer (a counterexample in itself), but counting it would re-resolve in the window a problem that was already resolved.
